summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain and found to be in alcohol withdrawal, with new-onset atrial fibrillation and suspected untreated pneumonia. He had a history of coronary artery disease with stents, heart failure, and polysubstance abuse. Labs and imaging ruled out acute myocardial infarction, but an echocardiogram showed reduced ejection fraction at 25–30%. He was treated with benzodiazepines for withdrawal, antibiotics for pneumonia, and restarted on aspirin and lisinopril. Despite counseling on the risks, he chose to leave against medical advice. He was discharged with a prescription for levofloxacin and instructions to follow up with his primary care provider for ongoing management of heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and substance use.
